data.title: The Bet Vertex Pharmaceuticals Holders Made
data.description:
If you only glanced at the headlines on Vertex Pharmaceuticals over the past year, the story might have looked muddled. Revenue pushed ahead while net margin in Q3 2026 dropped to 19.0% from 35.2% the year before, and investors fretted over a US$10b acquisition and gene therapy costs. Holding Vertex Pharmaceuticals over the past year would have returned 23.2%, including dividends. If you were weighing that decision a year ago, what did the early data really suggest about this mix of growth and pressure?

Vertex Pharmaceuticals has already moved. See which of 32 high quality undervalued stocks still trade below our estimates.

The Argument You Would Have Been Weighing On Vertex Pharmaceuticals

The shares cost US$435 at the start of the period, so you were effectively choosing between two very different stories about where Vertex Pharmaceuticals might head next.

On the optimistic side, one camp saw a Fair Value of US$480, a notional price based on assumptions that revenue could grow 9.4% a year and profit margin might reach 37.4% as gene editing and new therapies scaled.

The pessimistic view pointed to a Fair Value of US$330, a scenario where tighter drug pricing, high gene therapy costs, and heavy R&D spending risked compressing returns despite any pipeline progress.

What The Results Changed For Vertex Pharmaceuticals

The Crinetics deal and growing breadth of ALYFTREK, CASGEVY, Journavx and Palsonify supported parts of the optimistic Vertex Pharmaceuticals story around diversification and new franchises. The same period showed pressure on profitability as total revenue reached US$3,440.8m in Q3 2026 while net income was US$653.6m and net margin fell to 19.0%. The evidence pointed in both directions.

The central question here was not headlines about new therapies, but whether expanding into gene therapy and endocrinology could support margins. When you look at another drug developer, test the same claim directly against reported net income and margin rather than only watching top line progress or pipeline headlines.

What Today's Vertex Pharmaceuticals Price Already Assumes

Vertex Pharmaceuticals now trades at US$539, with this Narrative's Fair Value sitting below that level according to the bearish analyst Narrative on Simply Wall St. Over the past year, the share price gain of 23.2% leaves less room for forgiving missteps.

The Narrative argues that at this price, you need confidence that new pillars like CASGEVY, renal programs and Crinetics assets can scale into high margin franchises despite heavier spending. The key assumption a buyer must test is whether broader infrastructure and patient support costs can be absorbed while still lifting long term profitability.

"The main thing that has to go right is that Vertex Pharmaceuticals converts its expanded multi pillar portfolio, including CASGEVY, renal programs, acute pain, and endocrinology assets from Crinetics, into durable high margin franchises that justify the current premium attached to the stock. The numbers on guidance, acquisitions, and pipeline scale imply a share price that already bakes in successful diversification beyond cystic fibrosis and strong long term execution, leaving limited room for disappointment."

That disagreement has a full argument behind it. → Uncover the lower Fair Value this Narrative argues for

Another Pillar Behind Drug Pipelines

Looking past Vertex Pharmaceuticals, you can ask the same question elsewhere. What supports a drug portfolio when one flagship therapy ages?

One large healthcare group is leaning on a crowded pipeline instead. It is advancing treatments in cancer, heart health, respiratory care and infectious disease.

The strategy is not just adding products. Longer lasting regimens and more convenient dosing aim to keep patients on therapy.

This business is also using AI to refine drug discovery. That could reshape how many late stage projects it manages at once.

If that mix of breadth, duration and efficiency holds, your checklist beside Vertex may change significantly.

data.title: Revenue Miss: BFF Bank S.p.A. Fell 9.4% Short Of Analyst Revenue Estimates And Analysts Have Been Revising Their Models
data.description:
There's been a major selloff in BFF Bank S.p.A. (BIT:BFF) shares in the week since it released its interim report, with the stock down 26% to €1.46. Results look mixed - while revenue fell marginally short of analyst estimates at €179m, statutory earnings were in line with expectations, at €0.19 per share. This is an important time for investors, as they can track a company's performance in its report, look at what experts are forecasting for next year, and see if there has been any change to expectations for the business. Readers will be glad to know we've aggregated the latest statutory forecasts to see whether the analysts have changed their mind on BFF Bank after the latest results.

Trump has pledged to "unleash" American oil and gas and these 15 US stocks have developments that are poised to benefit.

After the latest results, the four analysts covering BFF Bank are now predicting revenues of €393.0m in 2026. If met, this would reflect a meaningful 11% improvement in revenue compared to the last 12 months. Per-share earnings are expected to jump 421% to €0.61. Before this earnings report, the analysts had been forecasting revenues of €425.1m and earnings per share (EPS) of €0.81 in 2026. The analysts seem less optimistic after the recent results, reducing their revenue forecasts and making a pretty serious reduction to earnings per share numbers.

View our latest analysis for BFF Bank

The consensus price target fell 13% to €2.64, with the weaker earnings outlook clearly leading valuation estimates. That's not the only conclusion we can draw from this data however, as some investors also like to consider the spread in estimates when evaluating analyst price targets. The most optimistic BFF Bank analyst has a price target of €4.45 per share, while the most pessimistic values it at €1.80. We would probably assign less value to the analyst forecasts in this situation, because such a wide range of estimates could imply that the future of this business is difficult to value accurately. With this in mind, we wouldn't rely too heavily the consensus price target, as it is just an average and analysts clearly have some deeply divergent views on the business.

Another way we can view these estimates is in the context of the bigger picture, such as how the forecasts stack up against past performance, and whether forecasts are more or less bullish relative to other companies in the industry. It's clear from the latest estimates that BFF Bank's rate of growth is expected to accelerate meaningfully, with the forecast 23% annualised revenue growth to the end of 2026 noticeably faster than its historical growth of 1.5% p.a. over the past five years. By contrast, our data suggests that other companies (with analyst coverage) in a similar industry are forecast to grow their revenue at 1.6% per year. It seems obvious that, while the growth outlook is brighter than the recent past, the analysts also expect BFF Bank to grow faster than the wider industry.

The Bottom Line

The biggest concern is that the analysts reduced their earnings per share estimates, suggesting business headwinds could lay ahead for BFF Bank. They also downgraded BFF Bank's revenue estimates, but industry data suggests that it is expected to grow faster than the wider industry. The consensus price target fell measurably, with the analysts seemingly not reassured by the latest results, leading to a lower estimate of BFF Bank's future valuation.

With that in mind, we wouldn't be too quick to come to a conclusion on BFF Bank. Long-term earnings power is much more important than next year's profits. At Simply Wall St, we have a full range of analyst estimates for BFF Bank going out to 2028, and you can see them free on our platform here..
